scope: FDM base models only; bundles, combos and resin excluded from the model count
findings: Official Anycubic store navigation lists Kobra 3 Max V2, Kobra 4, Kobra X, Kobra S1 Max and S1 bundles; this proves catalog presence, not launch chronology.
Official product pages read directly (Kobra 4, Kobra X, Kobra 3 Max V2) show prices, volumes and materials but no launch, preorder or shipping date for the printer itself.
Kobra X: Formnext 2025 debut; deposit program opened 2025-12-26 per a report of the Anycubic announcement; closing date not stated.
Kobra 4: revealed by Anycubic at RAPID+TCT 2026 (press release dated 2026-04-15) without the word launch; third-party review gives May 18, 2026; not confirmed by an official dated source.

Kobra 3 Max V2: official US page reads 'Ships in 24 hours' and lists Kobra OS; a search summary of a listing gives an estimated shipping window of Nov 15-25 that conflicts with that page; launch date unresolved (community forum 2026-08-28; third-party 'September 2026').
Kobra S1 Max: preorder covered in November 2025; launch date conflicts between 2025-11-05 and 2025-11-25 across third-party outlets; no official dated release found.
Firmware is named as Kobra OS on official pages, but no firmware version was studied; firmware is unknown.

Camera claims conflict: Kobra 4 official page states 720P camera with AI monitoring; Kobra 3 Max V2 has no built-in camera per a retailer FAQ summary and third-party sources, with a Live View Camera accessory on the official page.

LAN and cloud behaviour (LAN mode disabling cloud, app and AI detection; firmware updates requiring account binding) comes from third-party summaries and community projects only; not proven by official documentation read here.
Community MQTT ports 18910 and 9883 are reported for Kobra 3 and S1 stock firmware; not proven and not applied to the models in this report.
Telemetry and privacy terms were not read from the primary policy; summaries conflict and are not evidence.

Upload, start, pause, resume and cancel are recorded separately per model. Only Kobra 3 Max V2 start has an unverified search-summary claim (cloud print initiation, S16); every other command for every model is unknown, not unsupported.
No command was tested; no hardware, simulator, credentials or API access was used. Browser-Connector WebRTC and Connector safety checks are not affected by this research and were not evaluated.
gaps: Dated official launch or press release for Kobra 3 Max V2 is missing; ranking position 1 is provisional.
Dated official launch for Kobra 4 is missing; position 2 relies on third-party dates.
Kobra S1 Max launch date conflicts (2025-11-05 vs 2025-11-25); no official source.
Position 5 is unresolved: Kobra 3 V2 (May 15, year not confirmed) versus Kobra S1 base (pre-sale 2025-01-03).
Whether Kobra 3 Max V2 is a new base model or a revision of Kobra 3 Max (2024) is unresolved.
Firmware versions for every model are unknown.
LAN, cloud, authentication, MQTT and command protocol are not proven by official documentation.
Upload, pause, resume and cancel have no source for any model; start has only an unverified summary claim for Kobra 3 Max V2.
Telemetry, privacy and data-retention terms were not verified from the primary policy.
Licence of third-party firmware (Rinkhals) and access restrictions were not reviewed.
Three store and regional product pages returned HTTP 429 during retrieval; price and shipping data for Kobra S1 Max and Kobra 3 V2 remain unverified.
Search-summary sources were not opened as full pages; they support only the claims marked as third-party.

Read the Kobra S1 Max and Kobra 3 V2 product pages and compare them with the store listing.
Read the current Anycubic privacy policy and EU data statement from primary sources.
Read official manuals for each model to confirm LAN/cloud behaviour, firmware version and command support.
